devotions.citaat: What happened to you may not be your fault, but what you do with it is your responsibility. That is where forgiveness comes in.

zinnen.tekst: A couple of weeks ago, I preached a message on living in the fullness of forgiveness ... And I want to do a part two to that message this morning. Last time I spoke about the deep pain ... that we can get when people do things to us. ... And spoke about bringing that pain to God, bringing it into the light. ... Well, today I want to go over the foundations again of what I spoke about last time, but I want to expand on it in the practicalities of forgiveness. So I've got three points. The points are, number one, taking responsibility for your heart. Number two is trusting God with the justice. And number three, then dealing with the relationship.

Forgiveness is not about the relationship. And forgiveness is not about the other person. Forgiveness is actually what happens in you, what happens in your heart, the condition of your heart. Forgiveness is not saying that what happened was okay. Forgiveness is not saying that we forget what happened. But it's trusting God while we take responsibility for our heart to live in the freedom that we've been designed for. And I spoke about the example of being shot. If... If somebody were to shoot me, I can cry out for as long as I want. They shot me. ... It's not my fault that I was shot. It's their fault. They need to be held accountable. And I can be crying that out as long as I want while I'm bleeding out and will bleed to death. I can't take responsibility for somebody shooting me, but I can take responsibility for my wound and get myself to hospital so I don't die. ... You don't choose the wound, you don't cause the wound, but you can choose what you will do with that wound.

What happened to you may not be your fault, but what you do with it is your responsibility. That is where forgiveness comes in. ... Proverbs 4, verse 23. It says, Above all else, guard your heart. For everything you do flows from it. ... Forgiveness may not immediately remove the pain. But we can bring the pain to God. We can ask the Holy Spirit to heal us. And he does. It may not be immediate. It may take time. But he will heal. ... It's vitally important that we start with the fact that we have been forgiven by God. Jesus died for the forgiveness of our sins. ... Between us and God, it's good. ... He forgives us fully and completely so that we can rest in his presence, in his provision, in his purpose, the way he designed us to, the way it was in the beginning.

We live in you, we live in freedom, we live in life, we live in victory, we live in joy, in Jesus' mighty name ... Amen.

God is pleased when you forgive others. But not because of a religious obligation, because it frees you. It lets you live in the life that he created you for. When we hold unforgiveness in our hearts, we're thinking that we're holding the other person accountable. ... And we think, well, that's the right thing to do. But in doing so, we're doing the wrong thing. Jesus explains it in Matthew chapter 18.

Peter came to Jesus and asked, well, Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times. Jesus answered, I tell you, not seven times, but 77 times. Therefore, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants. ... A man who owed him 10,000 bags of gold was brought to him. And since he was not able to pay, the master ordered that he and his wife and his children and all that he had be sold to repay the debt. ... The servant's master took pity on him. He canceled the debt and let him go. But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred silver coins. He grabbed him and began to choke him. Pay back what you owe me, he demanded. ... The master called the servant in. You wicked servant, he said, I cancelled all that debt of yours because you begged me to. Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you? And in his anger his master handed him over to the jailers to be tortured until he should pay back all he owed. This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart.

On the surface of reading that, if you don't read it in the context of the rest of the scriptures, that can sound pretty harsh. But I want to tell you, you can trust God. ... See, if we trust in the forgiveness that we have in Christ, if we live in the forgiveness that we have, that we trust that God, we trust him for ultimate justice, it changes the way we live. See, this man, he was forgiven of a debt greater than he could ever pay. ... But the forgiveness didn't get in his heart. He didn't live with forgiveness in his heart. And so in his unforgiveness, it ruled him. ... Ephesians chapter 4, verses 26 to 27 says, In your anger, do not sin. Don't let the sun go down while you're still angry. Don't give the devil a foothold. ... Forgiveness frees you. Unforgiveness will imprison you. It's unforgiveness that imprisons you, not what the other person did to you that imprisons you.

Micah chapter 6 verse 8, I think explains it well. It says, He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? ... devotions.citaat: Forgiveness is different to reconciliation. Forgiveness takes just one person. Reconciliation takes two.

zinnen.tekst: And Jesus came. Thinking, what about the justice? Well, Jesus came and didn't answer the question philosophically. He came and he entered into the suffering for us. His suffering is greater than we could imagine. He paid the debt that we couldn't pay ourselves. And maybe we don't fully understand how things work eternally, except it's clear that justice belongs to God, and we can trust him with that. All right, let's get practical. How then do we deal with the relationship? ... Does forgiveness mean that we need to reconcile the relationship? Does forgiveness mean that we should trust them again? What if they're not sorry or don't change? ... What about justice? Well, these are the questions, right? Listen, forgiveness is different to reconciliation. Forgiveness takes just one person. Reconciliation takes two. Forgiveness may lead to reconciliation ... but it's not reconciliation. Reconciliation is pretty hard without forgiveness.

One of the things about forgiveness is it does empower us as we take responsibility. ... It moves us from the place of being a victim, blaming others, putting the power in their hands, to having agency yourself, to be empowered yourself. When we blame others, we are completely disempowered. But forgiveness puts us back in the place of power over our own lives, agency over our own lives. And not only that, but we have been forgiven. We are children of God. We're loved. We're accepted by God at a whole other level. From the place that we enter into in our relationships, we are loved by God. So from that place we are able to be the bigger person. We're able to enter into that relationship from a place of love. God's love. A supernatural love.

If I think about primary school, and I think about the bullies in primary school when I was at school ... And if I were to go back as I am today, not necessarily as big physically, but the bigness that is within is different to when I was a kid. And if I entered into school today and got bullied as I am today, I would respond totally differently. ... I'm a bigger person. Internally. We can enter into the relationships as the bigger person. So we take responsibility for our own heart. We let others take responsibility for their heart. I mean, their ugly actions usually reflect something ugly in their heart, and they're constantly living with that. We're the recipients only momentarily. ... Do we need to have a relationship with them? Well, there's plenty of people on the planet. But we can still choose to love them. That's our choice. Our hearts can be free. We don't have to allow their actions to determine our character. ... We can be people of love. We can be people of forgiveness. We can be people of grace. We can be people of power.

zinnen.tekst: So does that mean I should trust the person again? Well, here's the thing. We are empowered. We can choose whether we trust or whether we don't trust. Listen, forgiveness doesn't change the other person. It changes you. Wisdom says trust needs to be earned. ... When I look at how God treats us, it's like he does entrust us with his kingdom, with his plan, but he also puts provision in place for our sin and he takes ultimate responsibility for what he's entrusted to us. So he recognizes that we are going to fail. ... Wisdom says we can put boundaries in place. ... By allowing ourselves to trust God and to forgive, our hearts are empowered. We have choice. ... But forgiveness means we carry a clean heart. That our relationship with God empowers us with love, grace, and wisdom for the relationship.

So what do I do with the pain? What do I do with the pain? Bring it to God. ... And when you bring it into the light, things can change. Let the Holy Spirit heal you. ... My final thought on the relationship part is this. When you forgive somebody, I would encourage you to make a decision to pray for them. Pray for them. When you've got a free heart, a clean heart, a pure heart ... when your heart is free from their actions or their character, you can pray for them. ... They need your prayers. They need our prayers. And they need healing. So we say, God, I'm going to trust you with this. I surrender to you because I trust you. Even if I don't fully understand, I know that you're good. I know that you love me. I know that you're for me. I release it into your hands. I trust you with justice. I trust you with my heart. Ultimately, I trust you fully.

We all live in this fallen world. ... We all interact with people, and the people that we interact with are not perfect. ... People have hurt us. Some people have done it intentionally. That we can choose to live from a higher place, a relationship with God, knowing that we are fully loved, we are fully accepted in Christ, while we are fully seen. That the debt that Jesus has forgiven us of is actually an eternal one. It's far greater than the debt that we feel others owe us.

I prayed at the beginning of this service that this would not just be another Sunday, just another service, but that we would leave here free. Transformed. Jesus has done the hard work. As far as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are God's ways higher than ours. Do not let yourself stay imprisoned by the torment of your unforgiveness, resentment, bitterness. But live in the freedom that God gives us.

Jesus said, The enemy or the thief comes to steal and kill and destroy. But he said, I've come that you may have life and life to the full. Jesus died on the cross for the forgiveness of sins. He took upon himself anything that would separate us from God. Three days later, he rose from the dead, proving who he is. And to give us this new life, this life in relationship with God. Your past does not need to determine your future. But your relationship with God can. And it's not just for this lifetime. We're talking about eternity. ... Jesus died that you can be reconciled with God. You can live in relationship with God from this day forward. Jesus died for the forgiveness of your sins. So you can live God's way. You can live the life that you were designed for.

delen.citaat: You don't choose the wound, you don't cause the wound, but you can choose what you will do with that wound.
delen.uitleg: This is part two of a message on forgiveness, with three points: taking responsibility for your heart, trusting God with the justice, and dealing with the relationship. The first point opens with the picture of being shot: you can keep crying out that it was their fault and bleed to death, or you can take responsibility for your wound and get yourself to hospital. He quotes Proverbs 4:23: guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it. Forgiveness may not remove the pain at once, but you can bring the pain to God and ask the Holy Spirit to heal you. The place to start is that Jesus died for the forgiveness of our sins, so between us and God it is good.
delen.vraag: Where is there a wound you are still carrying, and what would it be like to bring that pain to God this week?

delen.titel: Let His Forgiveness Reach Your Heart
delen.citaat: But the forgiveness didn't get in his heart. He didn't live with forgiveness in his heart. And so in his unforgiveness, it ruled him.
delen.uitleg: Forgiving others is not a religious obligation to please God; God is pleased when we forgive because it frees us. He reads the whole parable of Matthew 18:21–35: a servant forgiven a debt greater than a lifetime of earnings chokes a fellow servant over a hundred silver coins. The forgiveness never got into that man's heart, so his unforgiveness ruled him. With Ephesians 4:26–27 he warns not to give the devil a foothold, because unforgiveness quickly becomes resentment and bitterness. If we trust in the forgiveness we have in Christ, it changes the way we live: forgiveness frees you, unforgiveness imprisons you.
delen.vraag: Jesus has cancelled a debt you could never pay; how is that forgiveness changing the way you live, and where has it not yet reached your heart?

delen.citaat: We forgive, not because they deserve freedom, but because we do.
delen.uitleg: Forgiving looks unfair when you look at the situation in isolation, but unforgiveness imprisons you in your own torment, and hurt people hurt people until we focus on what Jesus has done for us. Choosing unforgiveness is choosing a world of justice over mercy, and God will let you live in the world you choose. Micah 6:8 is his frame: act justly, love mercy, walk humbly with your God, which means trusting God with the justice instead of holding someone accountable yourself. Forgiveness acknowledges the hurt and the debt, and then releases it into God's hands. The devil wants us to question whether we can trust God; against that he puts being fully seen, fully loved and fully accepted in Christ.
delen.vraag: What kind of world do you want to live in, and what would it take for you to release the debt into God's hands this week?

delen.titel: From a Place of God's Love
delen.citaat: We don't have to allow their actions to determine our character.
delen.uitleg: Jesus did not answer the question of justice philosophically; He entered into the suffering for us and paid the debt we could not pay, so justice belongs to God. Then he turns to the practical questions people asked after the previous message. Forgiveness is different from reconciliation: forgiveness takes one person, reconciliation takes two. Forgiveness puts us back in the place of agency over our own lives, and because we are forgiven and loved by God at a whole other level we can enter a relationship as the bigger person, from God's love. We let others take responsibility for their own heart, and we can still choose to love them.
delen.vraag: How does knowing you are forgiven, loved and accepted by God change the way you walk into a difficult relationship?

delen.titel: I Trust You With My Heart
delen.citaat: Listen, forgiveness doesn't change the other person. It changes you.
delen.uitleg: Forgiveness does not mean trusting the person again; wisdom says trust needs to be earned, the way God entrusts us while making provision for our failure. Nor does it rule out boundaries: you do not have to be a doormat, and legal justice is a separate matter. What you do with the pain is bring it to God and let the Holy Spirit heal you, and his final thought is to pray for the person who hurt you, because they need healing too. It ends in a prayer of surrender: God, I trust you with justice, I trust you with my heart. Standing, he reminds everyone that this is a daily decision, and that the debt Jesus has forgiven us is an eternal one, far greater than what others owe us.
delen.vraag: What would it mean for you to pray for the person who hurt you, trusting God with the justice and with your heart?

delen.titel: Jesus Has Done the Hard Work
delen.citaat: Jesus has done the hard work. The devil, if he has his way, he'll have you not believing you can trust God. Not knowing you can trust God. But you can.
delen.uitleg: Today we choose to live in forgiveness, in His empowerment, love and grace, and to love mercy above justice, because we want what Jesus came to bring. Instead of an altar call for a few, he prays for the whole church, because every one of us is dealing with this: Jesus has done the hard work, God loves you and is for you, so do not stay imprisoned by torment. During the worship he reads Exodus 33:19 about God's mercy and compassion passing by. Then he speaks to anyone who has never received forgiveness from God: that is why Jesus came, and he quotes John 10:10, life to the full. Jesus died for the forgiveness of sins and rose again, so your past does not have to determine your future, but your relationship with God can, and he leads the whole room in a prayer to accept that.
delen.vraag: Where do you need to hear today that Jesus has done the hard work, and what would it look like to receive His forgiveness and live from that relationship?

luister.citaat: We forgive, not because they deserve freedom, but because we do.

uitnodiging.tekst: At the end he turns to anyone who has never received forgiveness from God, asks them to raise a hand, and leads the whole church in a prayer to accept what Jesus has done and to start life in relationship with God.
uitnodiging.citaat: Dear Jesus, thank you for what you've done for me. I accept that you died for me, for the forgiveness of my sins, and that You rose again to give me this new life, life in relationship with God.

gebedspunten.tekst: Thank You, Jesus, that You paid the debt we could never pay, and that between us and God it is good.
Show us where we are still carrying a debt, and help us release it into Your hands and trust You with the justice.
Heal the pain, Holy Spirit, and give us a clean heart so that we can pray for the people who hurt us.

gebeden.tekst: Holy Spirit, we thank you for your presence right now. God, we thank you for your love and grace. We thank you for the forgiveness of our sins, that you've paid for them all. And Lord, as we live in this world of brokenness, that you came in full of love, full of grace, showing us the truth of who you are. Our lives are in your hands, Lord. Where other people have hurt us, Lord, today we recognize the unforgiveness. We bring it to you, Lord. We acknowledge the debt, but Lord, we release it to you. We trust you with it. Lord, I pray for freedom this morning. Freedom, Lord. Lord, where people are struggling with torment, that they be released right now in Jesus' name. Released from the torment. Released from the tormentor. Lord, we give it to you. We choose freedom, we choose healing, we choose life. Lord, it doesn't mean we forget. It doesn't mean what they did is okay. It doesn't mean we need to be reconciled necessarily. It doesn't mean we have to trust them. But Lord, we choose life. And we choose to live in love. We choose to live empowered by you. The bigness of life. Eternal life. Our relationship with you. We just command any tormentors to be gone in Jesus' name. Freedom, joy, victory, wholehearted life. The life that we have in Jesus. A life of passion. A life of wholeheartedly living with the presence of God and the purpose of God in our hearts. Lord, free from needing to continue to protect ourselves. Lord, knowing that, Lord, we do guard our hearts, but Lord, we live in you, we live in freedom, we live in life, we live in victory, we live in joy, in Jesus' mighty name ... Amen.

Dear Jesus, thank you for what you've done for me. I accept that you died for me, for the forgiveness of my sins, and that You rose again to give me this new life, life in relationship with God. And I thank You that my past will no longer determine my future, but my relationship with God will. I choose to live Your way and step into the fullness of life that You died to give me. Amen.

Lord Jesus, man, we're so grateful for a wonderful, beautiful time in your presence today. Lord Jesus, what a beautiful thing that we can step into your forgiveness, that we can receive your forgiveness, your freedom for this beautiful life that we are called to live, to be ambassadors of that very forgiveness ourselves. So Lord Jesus, I actually pray that you would give us the strength this week to forgive where we need to, to let go, where we need to live in freedom, where we are called to. And Lord Jesus, where we step into our workplaces or our schools, our connect groups or our friend group situations, Lord, we know you go ahead of us. And so we walk in boldness and in courage and in life that you has called us to live in. In the mighty name of Jesus, we all pray. Amen.
